name: Good Morning Squat Hybrid
description: The good morning squat hybrid begins in a squat stance but hinges the torso deeply forward during the descent (resembling a good morning), then drives back to upright by extending both the hips and knees together. It simultaneously loads the erector spinae, glutes, and hamstrings through a range of motion that blends both exercises, increasing total posterior chain recruitment and training spinal erector endurance under axial load.

execution.starting_position: Barbell in a high-bar back squat position. Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
execution.setup_instructions: Begin with a moderate load — this is a technique and endurance lift, not a max squat. Ensure the barbell is seated high on the traps.
steps: Step 1: Begin standing with barbell on the upper traps.
Step 2: Simultaneously hinge the hips back and descend into a squat, allowing the torso to lean forward significantly.
Step 3: At the bottom, the torso should be at 45 degrees or more of forward lean.
Step 4: Drive up by extending hips and knees simultaneously, restoring upright torso.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descent. Exhale on the drive to the top.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom — the erector spinae must maintain spinal extension
Insufficient hip hinge — the torso should lean significantly more than a standard squat
safety_considerations: High demand on the spinal erectors — build up gradually and avoid with lower back injuries
Do not use a load that compromises neutral spine maintenance at the bottom
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full depth squat with significant forward torso lean to fully upright at the top.
coaching_cues: Let the chest fall toward the thighs on the way down
Drive the hips and chest up simultaneously on the way back
